title: Projection, sorting and limit
summary: Choose which fields to return and order, skip and limit the results to build pages.

docs.title: MongoDB: Project fields to return from a query

quiz.q: Which call returns the students with the **highest** marks first?
quiz.explain: `-1` means descending (largest first) and `1` means ascending. `limit` only takes a number.

quiz.q: Complete the call so that at most 5 students come back.
quiz.explain: `limit(n)` caps the number of documents returned.

quiz.q: The `scores` collection holds the values 10, 20, 30, 40 and 50 in a field called `v`. What does this return? Type the values separated by spaces.
quiz.explain: After sorting you have 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. `skip(1)` drops 10, and `limit(2)` keeps the next two.

quiz.q: Put the pieces in order to build a query for the three best students that shows only name and marks.
quiz.explain: Start with the collection, call `find` with the filter and projection, then chain `sort` and `limit`.
You cannot mix including (`1`) and excluding (`0`) fields in one projection. Only `_id` may be excluded together with included fields.

exercise.task:
The leaderboard shows 3 students per page, best marks first. Write the query for **page 2**.

- Sort by `marks` from highest to lowest.
- Skip the first page and keep 3 students.
- Show only `name` and `marks`, and hide `_id`.
hints: Chain `.sort(...)`, `.skip(...)` and `.limit(...)` after `find`. The second argument of `find` is the projection.
Page 2 with 3 per page means `skip(3)` and `limit(3)`. Sort descending with `{ marks: -1 }`.
